source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: Upstate: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$1.91/MWh on average) and lightest in Summer (−$0.07/MWh).
Lower Hudson Valley: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$7.39/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$1.51/MWh).
New York City: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$12.07/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$2.29/MWh).
Long Island: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$16.71/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$4.50/MWh).
In New York City, congestion peaks at 5–6 pm in July (−$80.16/MWh) and at 7–8 pm in January (−$40.11/MWh).
Weekdays are more congested than weekends in 10 of 11 zones. The biggest gap is J · New York City: −$6.67/MWh on weekdays vs −$4.53/MWh on weekends.
Of New York City's 10 worst days, 7 were in Winter and 8 fell on weekdays. The worst was 2025-07-01 (Tuesday) at −$192.59/MWh.
Worst single months: K · Long Island in Feb 2023 (−$43.24/MWh); J · New York City in Jan 2025 (−$36.31/MWh); F · Capital in Feb 2023 (−$33.38/MWh).
cannot_conclude: Seeing congestion peak in a season or hour does not tell us why; weather, demand, outages and fuel prices all change at the same time.
Daily and monthly averages hide 5-minute spikes; the worst moments are much more extreme than these averages.
data_notes: D · North: congestion is exactly 0 for all of December 2025 (average, minimum and maximum). This may be a data gap, so that month is not interpreted.
